category: CFD: Turbulent Nonisothermal and Reacting Flow, Thin-Film Flow, Shallow Water and Slip Flow
description: CFD Module and Mixer Module multiphysics interfaces for turbulent heat and mass transfer (turbulent Prandtl/Schmidt models, thermal and mass-transport wall functions, turbulent reaction closures, rotating-machinery variants), Thin-Film Flow (Reynolds equation, cavitation, rarefied gas films, squeeze-film damping), the time-explicit Shallow Water Equations, and the Microfluidics Module Slip Flow interface for rarefied gases.

tools.name: Nonisothermal Flow, Turbulent Flow Interfaces (CFD Module)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interfaces under Fluid Flow > Nonisothermal Flow that combine Heat Transfer in Fluids with a Turbulent Flow interface (Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, k-ε, realizable k-ε, k-ω, SST, low-Re k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras, v2-f, Wilcox R-ω, SSG-LRR, Elliptic Blending R-ε) or an LES interface, joined by the Nonisothermal Flow coupling. They model forced and natural convection with turbulent heat transport, thermal wall functions, pressure work and viscous heating.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Nonisothermal Flow > Turbulent Flow > (model); Java: physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowSST", "geom1"); physics().create("ht", "HeatTransferInFluids", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("nitf1", "NonIsothermalFlow", 3)

parameters.name: Turbulence model
parameters.description: Chosen by the interface entry; RSM models allow anisotropic turbulent conductivity.

parameters.name: Heat transport turbulence model
parameters.description: Kays–Crawford (default), Extended Kays–Crawford or user turbulent Prandtl number.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Stationary/Time Dependent with Initialization (wall distance) or One-Way NITF variants.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (some turbulence models also with the Heat Transfer Module). The coupling triggers pseudo time stepping for stationary solves.

tools.name: Conjugate Heat Transfer, Turbulent Flow Interfaces (CFD Module)
tools.description: Predefined interfaces under Heat Transfer > Conjugate Heat Transfer that couple Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids with laminar or any turbulent flow model through Nonisothermal Flow, so heat conduction in solid parts and convection in the fluid are solved together. They are the standard setup for heat sinks, cold plates, heat exchangers and electronics cooling.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Heat Transfer > Conjugate Heat Transfer > Laminar Flow / Turbulent Flow > (model)

parameters.name: Solid and Fluid domains
parameters.description: Heat Transfer in Solids and Fluids has Solid and Fluid nodes; the flow interface is active only in fluid domains.

parameters.name: Thermal wall functions
parameters.description: Standard or high viscous dissipation at walls.

tools.notes: Available with the CFD or Heat Transfer Module; turbulence models beyond k-ε/SST/algebraic need the CFD Module.

tools.name: Heat Transport Turbulence Models: Kays–Crawford and Anisotropic Conductivity (Nonisothermal Flow)
tools.description: Settings of the Nonisothermal Flow coupling that define the turbulent thermal conductivity. For RANS-EVM models a turbulent Prandtl number model is used (Kays–Crawford default, Extended Kays–Crawford with Re∞, or a constant Pr_T); for RSM models an anisotropic turbulent thermal conductivity (Daly–Harlow, Abe–Suga or user defined) is available, and the Elliptic Blending R-ε model always uses it.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Nonisothermal Flow > Heat Transfer Turbulence Model; fluid-side Java: physics("spf").prop("TurbulenceModelProperty").set("ThermalTurbType", "ExtendedKaysCrawford")

parameters.name: ThermalTurbModel
parameters.description: TurbPrNumber or AnisotropicTurbCond (RSM only).

parameters.name: ThermalTurbType
parameters.description: KaysCrawford | ExtendedKaysCrawford | UserDefPrt.

parameters.name: AnisotropicCondModel
parameters.description: DalyHarlow | AbeSuga | UserDefinedTurbCond.

tools.notes: Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4 in the fluid interface's TurbulenceModelProperty group; the GUI shows them in the Nonisothermal Flow coupling node.

tools.name: Thermal Wall Functions (Turbulent Nonisothermal Flow)
tools.description: When the flow interface uses wall functions or automatic wall treatment, the Nonisothermal Flow coupling applies thermal wall functions that bridge the unresolved thermal boundary layer. The Standard option suits most cases; High viscous dissipation at wall adds boundary-layer viscous heating, required for fast internal flows in narrow passages or with very viscous fluids.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Nonisothermal Flow > Heat Transfer Turbulence Model > Thermal wall function; fluid-side Java: prop("TurbulenceModelProperty").set("ThermalWallFunction", "HighViscDiss")

parameters.name: ThermalWallFunction
parameters.description: Standard (default) or HighViscDiss.

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Only relevant for Wall functions or Automatic treatment.

tools.notes: For Low Re wall treatment the thermal boundary layer is resolved and no wall function is used.

tools.name: Boussinesq Approximation and Density Options (Nonisothermal Flow)
tools.description: For incompressible flow the Nonisothermal Flow coupling can apply the Boussinesq approximation: all properties at reference temperature and pressure while gravity acts on a density linearized in temperature, ρ = ρ0(1 - α_p(T - T0)). The density can alternatively come from the heat transfer interface, the fluid flow interface, a custom linearized density or a custom expression. With reduced pressure the hydrostatic part is removed.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Nonisothermal Flow > Material Properties > Boussinesq approximation / Specify density

parameters.name: Boussinesq approximation
parameters.description: Checkbox, available when Compressibility is Incompressible.

parameters.name: Specify density
parameters.description: From heat transfer interface (default), From fluid flow interface, Custom linearized density (ρ_ref, α_p), Custom.

parameters.name: Include gravity / reduced pressure
parameters.description: Set in the flow interface.

tools.notes: Valid only for small density variations (Δρ/ρ0 << 1). With LES an additional subgrid buoyancy contribution is included.

tools.name: Nonisothermal Flow, Brinkman Equations (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface adding Heat Transfer in Porous Media and Brinkman Equations joined by the Nonisothermal Flow coupling, for convection in porous media such as packed beds, geothermal reservoirs near wells, porous heat sinks and natural convection in insulation. Local thermal equilibrium or nonequilibrium models come from the heat transfer side.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Nonisothermal Flow > Brinkman Equations

parameters.name: Physics
parameters.description: br (PorousMediaFlowBrinkman) + ht (PorousMediaHeatTransfer) + NonIsothermalFlow coupling.

parameters.name: Porous material
parameters.description: Porosity, permeability and solid thermal properties.

tools.notes: Available with the CFD, Porous Media Flow or Subsurface Flow Module.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Nonisothermal Flow (Laminar and Turbulent)
tools.description: Mixer Module interfaces combining laminar or turbulent (Algebraic yPlus to v2-f) rotating machinery flow with Heat Transfer in Fluids through Nonisothermal Flow, for heated/cooled stirred tanks, pumps with viscous heating and fans. Frozen Rotor, Frozen Rotor with Initialization and Frozen Rotor, One-Way NITF studies are available, followed by transient sliding-mesh runs if needed.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Nonisothermal Flow > Rotating Machinery, Nonisothermal Flow > Laminar / Turbulent (model)

parameters.name: Rotating Domain
parameters.description: Rotor domains and speed.

parameters.name: Nonisothermal Flow coupling
parameters.description: Temperature-dependent properties, buoyancy, viscous heating.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frozen Rotor (with Initialization) or Frozen Rotor, One-Way NITF.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module (turbulent variants also the CFD Module).

tools.name: Reacting Turbulent Flow, Concentrated Species (k-ε, k-ω, SST, Low Re k-ε)
tools.description: CFD Module multiphysics interfaces combining a turbulent flow interface with Transport of Concentrated Species and the Reacting Flow coupling, for gas mixtures whose composition affects density and viscosity (combustion, CVD, gas mixing). The coupling adds turbulent mass transport (turbulent Schmidt number), mass-transport wall functions and turbulent reaction closures.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow > Turbulent Flow, k-ε (k-ω, SST, Low Re k-ε); Java: physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowkeps", "geom1"); physics().create("tcs", "ConcentratedSpecies", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("rf1", "ReactingFlow", 3)

parameters.name: Turbulent mass transport model
parameters.description: Kays–Crawford or user-defined turbulent Schmidt number.

parameters.name: Turbulent reaction model
parameters.description: Mean value closure or eddy-dissipation model (Magnussen–Hjertager).

parameters.name: Diffusion model
parameters.description: Mixture-averaged, Maxwell–Stefan or Fick's law (in tcs).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (plus Chemical Reaction Engineering for chemistry features).

tools.name: Reacting Turbulent Flow, Diluted Species (k-ε, k-ω, SST, Low Re k-ε)
tools.description: Multiphysics interfaces combining turbulent flow with Transport of Diluted Species via the Reacting Flow, Diluted Species coupling, for dilute solutes in liquids or trace species in gases: mixing tanks, disinfection basins, pollutant dispersion. The coupling synchronizes the velocity field and adds turbulent mass diffusivity and mass transport wall functions.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow, Diluted Species > Turbulent Flow, k-ε (etc.); Java: multiphysics().create("rfd1", "ReactingFlowDS", 3)

parameters.name: Turbulent Schmidt number
parameters.description: Model for turbulent mass diffusivity.

parameters.name: Wall functions
parameters.description: Added automatically on walls using wall functions.

tools.notes: Verified type string ReactingFlowDS (default tag rfd). Requires the CFD Module for turbulent variants.

tools.name: Turbulent Mass Transport and Mass Transport Wall Functions (Reacting Flow)
tools.description: Closure of the turbulent species fluxes in RANS reacting flow: a gradient model with turbulent diffusivity ν_T/Sc_T added to molecular diffusion, and mass-transport wall functions analogous to thermal wall functions, formulated with molecular and turbulent Schmidt numbers, that bridge the unresolved concentration boundary layer at walls with wall functions.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Reacting Flow / Reacting Flow, Diluted Species > Turbulent Mass Transport (applied automatically with RANS models)

parameters.name: Sc_T
parameters.description: Turbulent Schmidt number (Kays–Crawford or user value).

parameters.name: Wall functions
parameters.description: Automatic on boundaries where the flow uses wall functions.

tools.example: // GUI: Multiphysics > Reacting Flow, Diluted Species 1 > Turbulent Mass Transfer > Turbulent Schmidt number model: User defined, Sc_T = 0.7
tools.notes: Check that the wall lift-off (spf.delta_w) is small compared with geometric features that affect reactions at surfaces.

tools.name: Turbulent Reaction Models: Mean Value Closure and Eddy Dissipation (Reacting Flow)
tools.description: Options for the mean reaction rate in turbulent reacting flow: mean value closure evaluates kinetics at mean concentrations and temperature (valid for small Damköhler numbers, perfectly-stirred limit), while the eddy-dissipation model (Magnussen–Hjertager) limits the rate by the turbulent mixing time scale k/ε (or 1/ω) and the deficient reactant, suitable for fast nonpremixed combustion and fast liquid reactions.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Reacting Flow > Turbulent Reactions / Reaction Source Term (turbulent flow)

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Mean value closure or Eddy-dissipation.

parameters.name: α, β
parameters.description: Eddy-dissipation model parameters (defaults for gaseous combustion; calibrate for liquids).

parameters.name: Damköhler number
parameters.description: Guides the choice of model.

tools.example: // GUI: Multiphysics > Reacting Flow 1 > Reaction Source Term: Eddy-dissipation, alpha = 4, beta = 0.5
tools.notes: For the low-Re k-ε model the time scale k/ε is used without near-wall damping.

tools.name: High Mach Number Reacting Flow (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Coupling between a High Mach Number Flow interface, Transport of Concentrated Species and optionally Chemistry, used by the High Mach Number Reacting Laminar/Turbulent (k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras) Flow interfaces. It accounts for heat of reaction, enthalpy diffusion and species mass fluxes in the energy equation of compressible reacting gas flows (supersonic combustion, rocket nozzles with chemistry, hypersonic inlets).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > High Mach Number Reacting Flow > Laminar / k-ε / Spalart–Allmaras; Java: multiphysics().create("hmrf1", "HighMachNumberReactingFlow", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Fluid flow (hmnf), Species transport (tcs), Chemistry (optional).

parameters.name: Density synchronization
parameters.description: Without Chemistry the density is taken from tcs.

tools.notes: Verified type string HighMachNumberReactingFlow. A diluted-species variant (High Mach Number Reacting Flow, Diluted Species) also exists.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Reacting Flow (k-ε, k-ω, SST, Low Re k-ε)
tools.description: Mixer Module interfaces coupling rotating machinery turbulent flow with species transport and reactions, for continuous stirred-tank reactors, fermenters and reactive mixing in pumps. Frozen Rotor studies give quasi-steady conversion; transient sliding mesh resolves blade-passage effects.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Chemical Species Transport > Reacting Flow > Rotating Machinery, Reacting Flow > Turbulent Flow, k-ε (etc.)

parameters.name: Physics
parameters.description: Turbulent flow + Rotating Domain + Transport of Concentrated/Diluted Species + Reacting Flow coupling.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frozen Rotor with Initialization.

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module plus the CFD Module (and Chemical Reaction Engineering Module for detailed chemistry).

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, High Mach Number Flow (Laminar and Turbulent)
tools.description: Mixer Module interfaces combining compressible High Mach Number Flow (laminar, k-ε, Spalart–Allmaras, Algebraic yPlus, L-VEL, realizable k-ε, k-ω, SST, low-Re k-ε, v2-f) with Rotating Domains, for compressors, turbochargers and high-speed fans. Mixing planes and Frozen Rotor with Initialization are supported for stage calculations.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > Rotating Machinery, High Mach Number Flow > (model)

parameters.name: Rotating Domain
parameters.description: Rotor speed and axis.

parameters.name: Mixing Plane
parameters.description: HighMachNumberFlowMixingPlane between stages (3D).

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frozen Rotor with Initialization (adds Mixing Plane Initialization when needed).

tools.notes: Requires the Mixer Module plus the CFD Module.

tools.name: Thin-Film Flow, Domain (tff, 2D)
tools.description: Thin-Film Flow variant defined on a 2D domain that represents the plan view of a narrow gap: the Reynolds (liquid) or modified Reynolds (gas) equation is solved for the film pressure with wall and base heights, velocities and optional cavitation. It is convenient for slider bearings, seals and squeeze-film dampers drawn in 2D.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Thin-Film Flow > Thin-Film Flow, Domain (2D); Java: physics().create("tff", "ThinFilmFlowDomain", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid type
parameters.description: Liquid (Reynolds), Liquid with cavitation, Gas (modified Reynolds).

parameters.name: Reference surface normal orientation
parameters.description: Out of plane (default) or into plane.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid-Film Properties, Border, Initial Values.

tools.notes: Available with the CFD Module or MEMS Module.

tools.name: Thin-Film Flow, Edge (tff, 2D and 2D Axisymmetric)
tools.description: Thin-Film Flow interface on edges (boundaries) of 2D and 2D axisymmetric models: the film pressure varies along a line representing a narrow channel between two surfaces, for 1D bearing models, axisymmetric seals and elastohydrodynamic contacts with a 2D solid.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Thin-Film Flow > Thin-Film Flow (2D); Java: physics().create("tff", "ThinFilmFlowEdge", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid-Film Properties
parameters.description: Wall/base heights and velocities, viscosity, film flow model.

parameters.name: Border / Inlet / Outlet
parameters.description: End conditions for the film pressure.

tools.notes: The 3D shell version (ThinFilmFlowShell) is covered by the existing Thin-Film Flow, Shell entry.

tools.name: Fluid-Film Properties (Thin-Film Flow)
tools.description: Main node of the Thin-Film Flow interfaces defining the gap geometry (wall height above and base height below the reference surface plus additional displacements from structural interfaces), tangential wall and base velocities, fluid density (compressibility form) and viscosity, and the film flow model that relates mean velocity to pressure gradient and surface velocities (Poiseuille plus Couette).
tools.usage: Thin-Film Flow (tff) > Fluid-Film Properties (ffp1); Java: physics("tff").feature("ffp1").set("hw1", ...)

parameters.name: hw1 / hb1
parameters.description: Height of wall above and base below the reference surface (default 10 µm / 0).

parameters.name: uw / ub
parameters.description: Additional wall/base displacement (user defined or from a structural interface).

parameters.name: TangentialWallVelocity / TangentialBaseVelocity
parameters.description: Off, FromDeformation or userdef (vw, vb).

parameters.name: QchType (liquid) / QchTypeMR (gas)
parameters.description: Film flow model: NoSlip, Slip (slip lengths Lsw, Lsb), rarefied models Model1/Model2, userdef.

parameters.name: ForceModel
parameters.description: PressureOnly, CouetteOnly or PressureAndShear force on the surfaces.

tools.notes: Property names verified in COMSOL 6.4. The reference-surface normal decides which structure is the wall and which is the base.

tools.name: Liquid with Cavitation (Thin-Film Flow, Elrod Algorithm)
tools.description: Fluid type option of the Thin-Film Flow interfaces that models gaseous cavitation in lubricated bearings with a modified Elrod–Adams algorithm based on JFO theory: the solved variable switches between pressure in the full film and fluid fraction in the ruptured region, predicting film rupture and reformation. It enables realistic load capacity of journal bearings under heavy load.
tools.usage: Thin-Film Flow interface > Physical Model > Fluid type: Liquid with cavitation (Cavitation transition width)

parameters.name: Cavitation transition width
parameters.description: Smoothing width in pressure (default 1 MPa).

parameters.name: Starvation
parameters.description: Border/Inlet option with fluid fraction θ0 (default 0.6).

tools.example:
// GUI: Thin-Film Flow > Physical Model > Fluid type = Liquid with cavitation
// Application Library: CFD_Module/Thin-Film_Flow/journal_bearing_cavitation
tools.notes: Not suited when surface tension plays an important role; vapor cavitation at high-frequency loads is not addressed.

tools.name: Rarefied Gas Film Flow Models (Modified Reynolds Equation)
tools.description: For Gas fluid type the Thin-Film Flow interfaces solve the modified Reynolds equation and offer film flow models that correct the Poiseuille flow for rarefaction at high Knudsen numbers, including slip at walls and empirical fits to the linearized Boltzmann BGK solution (Fukui–Kaneko type models), with the mean free path from the material or user input and accommodation coefficients. This is essential for MEMS squeeze-film damping at low pressure and air bearings in hard disk drives.
tools.usage: Thin-Film Flow > Fluid-Film Properties > Film flow model (gas: QchTypeMR) and Mean free path

parameters.name: QchTypeMR
parameters.description: NoSlip | Slip | Model1 | Model2 | userdef | UserDefinedGen.

parameters.name: MeanFreePathRarefied / lambda0 / plambda0
parameters.description: Mean free path from material or user defined at a reference pressure.

parameters.name: alphaw / alphab / alphaboth
parameters.description: Tangential momentum accommodation coefficients.

tools.notes: Rarefied models apply only when Fluid type is Gas.

tools.name: Border (Thin-Film Flow)
tools.description: Default boundary condition at the edge of a thin film: zero pressure, prescribed pressure or a border flow condition accounting for the pressure drop as flow converges into the gap (absolute or relative acoustic elongation, out-of-plane motion model, or user-defined pressure gradient). Starvation is available with cavitation.
tools.usage: Thin-Film Flow > Border (bdr1); Java: physics("tff").feature("bdr1").set("BorderCondition", "BorderFlow")

parameters.name: BorderCondition
parameters.description: ZeroPressure | Pressure (pf0) | BorderFlow (| Starvation with cavitation).

parameters.name: ElongationType
parameters.description: Absolute (dL) | Relative (dLr) | out-of-plane_motion | UserDefined.

tools.notes: Border flow gives better damping predictions for small MEMS plates than zero pressure.

tools.name: Perforations (Thin-Film Flow)
tools.description: Feature modeling an array of etch holes in a MEMS plate or substrate as a distributed gas sink proportional to the pressure difference to the ambient, with the admittance given directly or computed by the Bao model for square or circular holes. It captures reduced squeeze-film damping of perforated microstructures.
tools.usage: Thin-Film Flow > Perforations; Java: physics("tff").create("perf1", "Perforations", 2)

parameters.name: Perforation admittance
parameters.description: User defined Y or Bao model.

parameters.name: Perforation shape
parameters.description: Square (side s_h) or Circular (radius r_h).

parameters.name: Hole length l_h / density n_h
parameters.description: Plate thickness and holes per area.

tools.notes: Applies only when walls have no tangential movement.

tools.name: Inlet and Outlet (Thin-Film Flow)
tools.description: Boundary conditions where lubricant enters or leaves the gap: zero pressure, prescribed pressure or normal inflow velocity (and Starvation with a fluid fraction when cavitation is active). Used for oil supply grooves and holes in journal and thrust bearings.
tools.usage: Thin-Film Flow > Inlet / Outlet; Java: physics("tff").create("inl1", "Inlet", 1)

parameters.name: Inlet condition
parameters.description: Zero pressure (default), Pressure p_film0, Normal inflow velocity U0, Starvation θ0.

parameters.name: Reference pressure
parameters.description: p_film0 is relative to p_ref unless p_ref = 0.

tools.notes: Point/edge/boundary dimension depends on the thin-film variant.

tools.name: Squeeze-Film Damping in the Frequency Domain (Thin-Film Flow)
tools.description: The Thin-Film Flow interfaces support frequency-domain (linearized) analysis: the Reynolds equation is linearized about a static offset so harmonic wall motion yields complex film pressures, damping and spring forces. Together with Solid Mechanics or Shell it predicts the quality factor of MEMS resonators and accelerometers.
tools.usage: Study > Frequency Domain (or Eigenfrequency with coupled structure); Thin-Film Flow Fluid type Gas

parameters.name: Linearization assumptions
parameters.description: Harmonic pressure much smaller than ambient; gap change much smaller than gap.

parameters.name: Absolute pressure
parameters.description: Set to p_ref in the frequency domain.

tools.notes: For large amplitudes use a time-dependent study instead.

tools.name: Thin-Film and Porous Media Flow (Multiphysics Coupling)
tools.description: Boundary coupling between a Thin-Film Flow interface and Darcy's Law, exchanging mass between a lubricating film and an adjacent porous layer. It models self-lubricating porous bearings, squeeze films next to porous plates and fluid exchange between fractures and matrix.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Thin-Film and Porous Media Flow; Java: multiphysics().create("tfpf1", "ThinFilmAndPorousMediaFlow", 2)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Thin-film flow (tff) and Porous media flow (dl).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries shared by the film and the porous domain.

tools.notes: Verified type string ThinFilmAndPorousMediaFlow.

tools.name: Shallow Water Equations, Time Explicit (swe)
tools.description: Time-explicit discontinuous Galerkin solver of the depth-averaged shallow water equations in 1D or 2D for water depth h and water flux q over a fixed bottom topography, with wetting and drying. It models dam breaks, tsunami run-up, floods, tidal and river flows where horizontal scales greatly exceed depth.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Shallow Water Equations > Shallow Water Equations, Time Explicit (swe); Java: physics().create("swe", "ShallowWaterEquationsTimeExplicit", "geom1")

parameters.name: Domain Properties
parameters.description: Bottom height and density.

parameters.name: Boundary nodes
parameters.description: Wall, Inlet, Outlet, Symmetry, Interior Wall.

parameters.name: Sources
parameters.description: Domain Source (momentum: friction, Coriolis, wind) and Water Source (height).

parameters.name: Force variables
parameters.description: swe.Fpx, swe.Fpy = hydrostatic pressure force per unit length on boundaries.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD or Subsurface Flow Module. Always time dependent; the time step follows the CFL condition based on wave speed sqrt(g h).

tools.name: Domain Properties (Shallow Water Equations)
tools.description: Domain node of the Shallow Water Equations interface defining the bottom topography (time-independent bottom height expression or interpolation of bathymetry data) and the density used for hydrostatic pressure and force evaluation.
tools.usage: Shallow Water Equations > Domain Properties (dp1)

parameters.name: Bottom height
parameters.description: Expression of x, y (e.g., interpolation function of bathymetry).

parameters.name: Density ρ
parameters.description: User defined (default 1000 kg/m³) or from material; not used in the solution itself.

tools.notes: Topography gradients should be resolved by the mesh.

tools.name: Domain Source and Water Source (Shallow Water Equations)
tools.description: Source nodes of the Shallow Water Equations: Domain Source adds a momentum source term (bottom friction such as Manning or Chezy expressions, Coriolis force, wind stress) and Water Source adds a height source to the continuity equation (rain, inflow from ground, evaporation losses).
tools.usage: Shallow Water Equations > Domain Source / Water Source; Java: physics("swe").create("ds1", "DomainSource", 2); create("ws1", "WaterSource", 2)

parameters.name: Momentum source
parameters.description: Vector source in the momentum equation (e.g., -g n^2 |q| q / h^(7/3) for Manning friction).

parameters.name: Water source
parameters.description: Height source rate (m/s).

tools.notes: The friction expression is user-defined; check dependent-variable names (h and q components) in the interface's Dependent Variables section.

tools.name: Inlet, Outlet and Wall (Shallow Water Equations)
tools.description: Boundary conditions of the time-explicit Shallow Water Equations using an HLLC Riemann solver: the Inlet prescribes water depth (or total height) and velocity or flux as primitive or conservative variables, the Outlet prescribes external states for sub- or supercritical outflow, and the Wall imposes weak no penetration (no boundary layer since viscosity is neglected).
tools.usage: Shallow Water Equations > Inlet (InletBoundary) / Outlet (OutletBoundary) / Wall (WallBC)

parameters.name: Input state
parameters.description: Primitive (h, u) or Conservative (h, q) variables.

parameters.name: Water depth
parameters.description: User defined, from domain values or total height H0.

parameters.name: Supercritical inlet
parameters.description: Both depth and flux must be specified.

tools.notes: Use swe.Fpx/swe.Fpy line integrals on walls to obtain hydrostatic loads on structures.

tools.name: Slip Flow (slpf)
tools.description: Microfluidics Module interface for gas flow in the slip regime (Knudsen number 0.01-0.1): Navier–Stokes and heat equations with Maxwell velocity slip, thermal creep and von Smoluchowski temperature jump boundary conditions that represent the Knudsen layer. It suits microchannels, MEMS gas flows and vacuum components at moderate rarefaction.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Rarefied Flow > Slip Flow (slpf); Java: physics().create("slpf", "SlipFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Neglect inertial term (Stokes flow)
parameters.description: For very low Reynolds number.

parameters.name: Reference pressure
parameters.description: Default 1 atm.

parameters.name: Default nodes
parameters.description: Fluid (NonIsothermalFlowModel), External Slip Wall, Initial Values.

tools.notes: Requires the Microfluidics Module. For Kn > 0.1 use the Molecular Flow Module (Transitional or Free Molecular Flow).

tools.name: External Slip Wall (Slip Flow)
tools.description: Default wall of the Slip Flow interface for boundaries external to the whole geometry: wall velocity, wall temperature and slip coefficients from Maxwell's model (tangential momentum accommodation) or user-defined thermal slip, viscous slip and temperature jump coefficients with standard or Sharipov mean free path definitions.
tools.usage: Slip Flow > External Slip Wall (eslw1); Java: physics("slpf").create("eslw2", "ExternalSlipWall", 2)

parameters.name: Velocity of moving wall u_w
parameters.description: Wall velocity vector.

parameters.name: Wall temperature T_w
parameters.description: Default 293.15 K.

parameters.name: Slip coefficients
parameters.description: Maxwell's model (a_v) or user defined σ_T, σ_S, ζ_T.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Weak (default) or Nitsche constraints.

tools.notes: Accommodation coefficients are typically 0.85-1.0.

tools.name: Slip Wall and Interior Slip Wall (Slip Flow)
tools.description: Slip Wall applies velocity slip and temperature jump on boundaries adjacent to solid domains where heat transfer is solved (temperature continuous with the solid), and Interior Slip Wall applies slip on both sides of thin interior walls. Together with External Slip Wall they cover all wall types in conjugate rarefied-gas problems.
tools.usage: Slip Flow > Slip Wall (SlipWall) / Interior Slip Wall (InteriorSlipWall)

parameters.name: Velocity of moving wall
parameters.description: Wall velocity.

parameters.name: Slip coefficients
parameters.description: Maxwell's model or user defined.

parameters.name: Constraint settings
parameters.description: Weak (default) or Nitsche.

tools.notes: Requires the Microfluidics Module.

tools.name: Microfluidic Wall Conditions (Free and Porous Media Flow)
tools.description: Wall condition of the Free and Porous Media Flow interface for microfluidic slip: a slip velocity boundary with a moving wall velocity, optional viscous slip (user slip length or Maxwell's model from TMAC and mean free path) and optional thermal creep. With the MEMS Module an electroosmotic velocity option is also available.
tools.usage: Free and Porous Media Flow, Brinkman (fp) > Microfluidic Wall Conditions

parameters.name: Use viscous slip
parameters.description: Slip length L_s (default 1e-7 m) or Maxwell's model (a_v 0.9, λ 1e-6 m).

parameters.name: Use thermal creep
parameters.description: Temperature and thermal slip coefficient (default 0.75).

parameters.name: Velocity of moving wall
parameters.description: Wall velocity.

tools.example: // GUI: Free and Porous Media Flow > Microfluidic Wall Conditions 1 > Use viscous slip: Maxwell's model, a_v = 0.9, lambda = 68[nm]
tools.notes: Available with the Microfluidics Module; Laminar Flow walls offer the same options through Wall > Slip velocity.

tools.name: Knudsen Number and Rarefied Flow Regimes
tools.description: Guide for choosing a gas flow interface by Knudsen number Kn = λ/l: continuum (Kn < 0.01, Laminar/Turbulent Flow), slip flow (0.01-0.1, Slip Flow or Navier–Stokes with slip walls), transitional (0.1-10, Transitional Flow lattice Boltzmann) and free molecular flow (Kn > 10, Free Molecular Flow angular coefficient method). The mean free path scales inversely with pressure.
tools.usage: Reference (Microfluidics Module User's Guide > Modeling Rarefied Gas Flows)

parameters.name: Kn
parameters.description: Mean free path over characteristic length.

parameters.name: λ
parameters.description: About 68 nm for air at 1 atm and room temperature.

tools.example: // Air at 100 Pa in a 10 um channel: lambda ~ 68e-9*101325/100 = 69 um -> Kn ~ 7 -> Transitional Flow (tran)
tools.notes: Choose the Molecular Flow Module for Kn > 0.1.

tools.name: Dimensionless Numbers in Microfluidics (Re, Pe, Ca, Bo, We, Oh)
tools.description: Reference of dimensionless groups that decide physics and solver stability in microfluidics: Reynolds and (cell) Péclet numbers govern stabilization needs; Bond/Eötvös, capillary, Weber and Ohnesorge numbers characterize two-phase flows; Dukhin for electrokinetics; Knudsen for rarefaction; Marangoni for thermocapillary flow; Mach for compressibility.
tools.usage: Reference (Microfluidics Module User's Guide > Dimensionless Numbers in Microfluidics); evaluate e.g. spf.cellRe in Results

parameters.name: Re, Pe
parameters.description: Cell values above 1 cause oscillations without stabilization.

parameters.name: Ca = μv/σ, Bo = ρgL²/σ
parameters.description: Capillary and Bond numbers for surface-tension-dominated flows.

parameters.name: We, Oh
parameters.description: Jet/droplet breakup regimes.

tools.example: // Droplet generator: mu = 1e-3 Pa*s, v = 0.01 m/s, sigma = 0.02 N/m -> Ca = 5e-4 (squeezing regime)
tools.notes: The Laminar Flow interface in the Microfluidics Module handles compressible flow up to Ma ≈ 0.3.
